spans.s:
Kūṭaka (EI 5), probably, headman of the cultivators; same as Grāmakūṭaka.
 (IE 8-5; EI 4, 26), tax for the maintenance of the Kūṭaka; see pravaṇikara-kūṭaka-prabhṛti-samast-ādāya (Ep. Ind., Vol. IV, p. 101).
 (CII 4), a measure of capacity.
 (EI 2), a load or measure of salt.
Kūṭakolasa (IE 8-3; EI 29), known from the Bhauma-Kara records of Orissa; official designation of uncertain import; cf. Kūṭa or Kūṭaka.
kūṭa-śāsana (EI 7; IA 30; BL), a forged charter.
Kūṭāyukta (EI 22), official designation; probably Kūṭa (Kūṭaka) and Āyukta.

kuṭī (IE 8-8), a factory; cf. nīla-kuṭī.
 (LL), a Buddhist temple; an abbreviation of gandhakuṭī.
kuṭumba-vṛtti, cf. Kannaḍa kuttumbitti (EI 18), gift of land for the maintenance of the donee's family.
kuṭumba-yātrā (EI 12; BL), name of a religious ceremony; [] a procession of the royal family to the temple of the family deity on the occasion of the king's coronation or a marriage in the palace.
Kuṭumbin (EI 12, 17, 23; SII 1), a cultivator; an agriculturist householder; a householder or ryot.
kuṭumbinī (EI 19; CII 2-1; ML), originally, ‘the wife of a householder’; later, ‘wife’ in general (cf. Sel. Ins., p. 164).
